script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

Title: A Second Chance at Life

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

A small, quaint coffee shop nestled in the heart of a bustling downtown area. FAMILY PATRICK sits at a table by the window, CHARLES in his late 50s, holding a newspaper, LUCY, mid-30s, reading a book, and JAMES, 8, drawing on a piece of paper.

CHARLES: (sighs) I can't believe how fast time flies.

LUCY: (smiling) It does, dear. Enjoy your coffee while it's still hot.

James looks up from his drawing, wide-eyed.

JAMES: Can I have a cookie, mom?

LUCY: (laughs) Sure thing, buddy.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS

The barista, SARA, mid-20s, hands a cookie to JAMES. She catches CHARLES' eye and gives him a warm smile.

SARA: Hi, Mr. Patrick. How are you today?

CHARLES: (smiling back) I'm doing well, thank you, Sara.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Back at the table, CHARLES turns to LUCY.

CHARLES: You know, I've been thinking about my old colleagues from work. I wonder what they're up to these days.

LUCY: Maybe you should reach out to them.

CHARLES: (hesitates) I don't know. It's been so long.

INT. OFFICE BUILDING - DAY

A flashback to CHARLES' old office building. He walks down the hall, past familiar faces, and stops in front of his old cubicle. He looks around, remembering the long hours spent here.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Back in the present, CHARLES takes out his phone and dials a number.

CHARLES: (into phone) Hi, Ann? It's Charles Patrick. Long time no see. (pauses) Yeah, I was just reminiscing about the old days and thought it would be nice to catch up. Would you be free for lunch sometime soon?

INT. ANN'S APARTMENT - DAY

ANN, early 60s, opens the door to her apartment. CHARLES stands nervously on her doorstep. They exchange warm hugs, catching up on lost time.

ANN: (laughs) I can't believe it's been so long since we last saw each other.

CHARLES: (smiling) Me neither.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

LUCY and JAMES join CHARLES and ANN for lunch at the coffee shop. They share stories, laughs, and memories.

CHARLES: (to JAMES) And this is my son, James. He's eight and in the third grade.

ANN: (smiling) Hello, James. What do you like to do?

JAMES: (excitedly) I like to draw, read, and play soccer.

INT. SOCCER FIELD - DAY

A scene of JAMES playing soccer in the park with his team and friends. CHARLES and LUCY watch proudly from the sidelines.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Back at the coffee shop, CHARLES, LUCY, and ANN finish their lunch, exchanging contact information.

ANN: It was so nice catching up with you, Charles. I'm glad we ran into each other.

CHARLES: Likewise, Ann. It feels like a second chance at life.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

As they leave the coffee shop, CHARLES and LUCY hold hands, looking content.

CHARLES: (to LUCY) I'm so glad we came here today.

LUCY: Me too. It feels like a new beginning.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

CHARLES sits at the same table by the window, now with ANN joining him, reading a book together. JAMES plays on the floor nearby, drawing.

CHARLES: (smiling) Life is full of surprises.

ANN: Indeed.

They share a warm glance, cherishing their second chance at life and the precious moments they've been given.

FADE OUT.
